subject: OPEN statement
notes:
kb/Work PB325 (landed). RULE (--check 14.9.27.4 "'X' at an intersection indicates that the specified statement, used in the access mode given for that row, may be used with the open mode given at the top of the column"): Table 20 licenses each (statement, access mode, open mode) triple; every BLANK cell is an unsuccessful execution whose status 9.1.13.7 names -- item 7 '47' for READ/START not open input or I-O, item 8 '48' for WRITE (a: access sequential and not open extend/output; b: access random or dynamic and not open I-O/output), item 9 '49' for REWRITE/DELETE RECORD not open I-O. Table 20 was read from the PDF (page 709) as well as the transcription, because the load-bearing signal here is a BLANK CELL and the OCR of a blank is not self-evident: Random x WRITE and Dynamic x WRITE carry X under Output and I-O only, and the Extend column of both rows is empty.
IMPLEMENTATION. The ACCESS MODE is the sole branch discriminator and lives in ONE place, KeyedConnector.Access (the abstract base RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector now share); the open mode is only ever the screen that follows. Each connector's Write opens with 'bool sequentialRelease = Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential', takes item 8 a)'s arm when true and item 8 b)'s when false; SequentialConnector.Write carries item 8 a) directly (12.4.5.5.2 SR2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for a sequential file); READ/START answer item 7 and REWRITE/DELETE item 9 in both keyed connectors and in SequentialConnector; the blank Random x START row is enforced one level up, at bind, by KeyedIoBinder.BindStart's 14.9.41.3 SR1 screen (COBOL0862).
EVIDENCE. conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_table20_seq_relative and conformance:cases/14.9.27-OPEN/l1_table20_indexed walk EVERY cell of Table 20 that conforming source can reach -- 4 open modes x {READ, WRITE, REWRITE, START, DELETE RECORD} over sequential, relative and indexed organizations at all three access modes, 139 observations, each expected value derived from Table 20 plus 9.1.13.7 items 7/8/9 and every one observed. conformance:cases/14.9.27-OPEN/pb325-start-random-access pins the blank Random x START row on BOTH keyed organizations at all four editions. The Random/Dynamic x WRITE x Extend cell is UNREACHABLE from conforming source -- 14.9.27.3 SR2 confines the EXTEND phrase to sequential access -- so it is pinned at the runtime by unit:Table20WriteOpenModeTests, whose four defect facts go RED if the open mode is put back into the branch predicate (measured) while its eight control facts stay green.
WHAT WAS FIXED. RelativeConnector.Write and IndexedConnector.Write selected the branch with '_access == KeyedAccess.Sequential || Mode == FileOpenMode.Extend'; the disjunct routed a random- or dynamic-access connector opened EXTEND into the sequential-release branch, whose own screen accepts extend, so the WRITE appended a record and reported '00' where item 8 b) requires '48'. That made a run-time answer depend on a bind-time syntax rule (SR2) that is enforced nowhere -- kb/Work PB318 -- so the runtime is now correct independently of it.
EDITIONS: Table 20 is version-invariant; the DELETE RECORD row for a sequentially-accessed relative/indexed file and the dynamic access mode ride the relative/indexed I-O modules present at every edition adjudicated here, and the negative fixture was observed rejecting at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023.
